fieldMarks: Colour ranges from black to nearly white with every shade of gray and tan; gray or black most common
Adult males in Interior Alaska mostly 38–52 kg; females about 5–7 kg lighter
behavior: Lives in packs, typically 6–7 (up to 20–30) animals, holding territories against other wolves
Howls to communicate, including warning other packs away
Preys mainly on moose, caribou or deer, with sheep, hares, beaver and other small prey
In the far northwest may follow migratory caribou; territories span hundreds to thousands of square kilometres
habitat: No particular habitat preference; persists best where road density and human access are low and ungulate prey is abundant.
range: Throughout much of Canada and Alaska. South of Canada limited to the northern Rockies (Montana, Idaho, Wyoming), the western Great Lakes (Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan's Upper Peninsula) and the Washington Cascades, with remnant reports in northern Mexico.
